solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Author offering a smaller version of the double-decker sandwich?

parts.note: a double-decker is a bus, and a car is a smaller road vehicle
a filled roll is a kind of sandwich

explanation.surface: Someone offers a slimmed-down version of a towering stacked sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double-decker sandwich' reads as one food, but the double-decker is a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll was the writer of the Alice books, so he is an example of an author.

clue.text: Empty copy right in mire, being enhanced by technology

indicators.note: an empty word keeps only its outside letters
in puts one piece inside another

parts.note: a bog is a mire

explanation.surface: A hollow copy stuck in the mud, upgraded by technology.
explanation.definitionFit: A part-human, part-machine creature is a person augmented by technology.

clue.text: Broadcast recalled about one country or another

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other
recalled means called back, so read backwards

parts.note: to air is to broadcast
Oman is a country

explanation.surface: A broadcast is withdrawn concerning one nation or another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one country or another' reads as one phrase, but 'one country' is wordplay and 'another' alone is the definition: a second country.
explanation.definitionFit: The Balkan state is another nation, following on from the one country already named.

clue.text: Standard old gun charged with bullets, sawn-off

indicators.note: a gun charged with something is loaded with it, so it goes inside

parts.note: a rifle is a gun

indicators.note: a sawn-off barrel is shortened, so the last letter goes

parts.note: ammo is ammunition, bullets

explanation.surface: An old shotgun is loaded with bullets and has its barrel sawn off.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the red-gold banner of the French kings, so a standard or flag.

clue.text: Sheltered side didn't use rough side

parts.note: the lee is the side sheltered from the wind

indicators.note: rough suggests something roughed up, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A team kept to the sheltered side and avoided the rough side of the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side' means a sports team; LEEDS UNITED is an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A side is a team in British sport, and this is a professional football club.

clue.text: Shooter's backfiring miss involving smoke

indicators.note: something backfiring goes the wrong way, so the assembled letters are read from the end
involving means one piece wraps round another

parts.note: a maid is an old word for a girl or miss
a cig is a cigarette, a smoke

explanation.surface: A gunman's weapon misfires, missing its target in a cloud of smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooter' and 'smoke' suggest a gun, but a shooter is also slang for a camera; 'backfiring' reads the letters right to left, giving MACIGID turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: A shooter is slang for a camera, and a digital camera is often shortened to this.

clue.text: Father of Mickey Mouse half abandoned Pluto

indicators.note: with half abandoned, only the front half of the name is kept

parts.note: Walt Disney created Mickey Mouse

explanation.surface: Mickey's creator half gave up on the dog Pluto.
explanation.walkthrough: Pluto looks like Mickey's dog, but it is the Roman god of the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman myth the ruler of the underworld goes by this name as well, as does his realm.

clue.text: Relish got distributed around America

indicators.note: around means one piece goes about another
distributed means spread about, so these letters are scattered

parts.note: US is short for the United States, America

explanation.surface: A tasty sauce was shipped across the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearty enjoyment or zest is relish in its sense of keen pleasure.

clue.text: Author on the radio to review old volume

indicators.note: something heard on the radio is only heard, so it signals a homophone

parts.note: to check is to review, O is old and V is volume, run together as one spoken word

explanation.surface: A radio critic sets out to review an old book.
explanation.walkthrough: CHECK, O and V said together sound like the Russian playwright's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Anton Chekhov was a Russian writer of plays and short stories.

clue.text: Dull king, nothing but dignified as a woman

parts.note: matt or mat means dull, not glossy
R is short for rex, king
nothing but means only, merely

explanation.surface: A dull king has nothing but a dignified woman for company.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes a stately, staid bearing in a middle-aged lady.

clue.text: Ship after poor wood, rough quality

indicators.note: after says the ship piece comes behind the other two

parts.note: bum is slang for poor or worthless
pine is a kind of wood
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A ship built from poor-quality timber turns out rough.
explanation.definitionFit: Unevenness of a surface is its bumpy character, a synonym for roughness.

clue.text: Novel and film featuring in one part of newspaper

parts.note: She is a novel by H. Rider Haggard
ET is Spielberg's film about an extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: A novel and a film are both reviewed in a newspaper section.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper is printed on large folded pages, each one being a single leaf of paper.

clue.text: Solid storing nitrogen from an organ

indicators.note: storing means holding something inside

parts.note: real means solid or substantial
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A solid sample containing nitrogen came from a bodily organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things relating to the kidneys, which are organs.

clue.text: Ancient burial site moved to Houston

indicators.note: moved signals the letters of the two words are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: An ancient burial site has been relocated to Texas.
explanation.walkthrough: SUTTON HOO is an Anglo-Saxon ship burial site in Suffolk, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Suffolk site holds a famous seventh-century ship burial, so it is an ancient grave site.

clue.text: Not this Marxist by tradition: someone very different!

parts.note: the opposite of this is that
Che Guevara was a Marxist revolutionary
a rite is a traditional ceremony

explanation.surface: A traditional Marxist is not this sort, but someone utterly unlike him.
explanation.walkthrough: A follower of Margaret Thatcher, Britain's right-wing prime minister, is the opposite of a Marxist.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of the free-market Conservative premier is a person poles apart from a Marxist.

clue.text: Australian native: I'm Satan, fiendishly — also satanic?

indicators.note: fiendishly suggests wild disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: and means also, in addition
satanic means evil

explanation.surface: An Australian creature boasts of being the devil himself, wicked too.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface doubles as a hint: the animal's name itself suggests a satanic fiend.
explanation.definitionFit: This carnivorous marsupial lives only on the island state south of mainland Australia, so it is a native animal.

clue.text: Taste small cake for starters, one … like this?

definitions.text: Taste small cake for starters, one … like this?

parts.note: a drop is a small taste of a drink

indicators.note: for starters means take the opening letter only

explanation.surface: An invitation to sample a little cake to begin with, one like this.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a small cake, perhaps served as a starter.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scotch pancake is a small griddle cake made from batter, a kind of little cake.

clue.text: I laugh out loud for the love of a child?

indicators.note: out loud means spoken aloud, so the words are heard

parts.note: I plus scream, something hilarious that makes one laugh

explanation.surface: Someone laughs aloud at a child's fondness.
explanation.walkthrough: I SCREAM said aloud sounds like the frozen treat, echoing the rhyme 'I scream, you scream'.
explanation.definitionFit: Children famously adore the frozen dessert, so it is what a child loves.

clue.text: Story in today's newspaper? Is that where the money is?

definitions.meaning: a report of what is happening now, an up-to-date story

definitions.text: Is that where the money is
definitions.meaning: a bank account in daily use, where one's money is held

explanation.surface: A reader wonders whether the money lies in today's news story.
explanation.definitionFit: A topical report is a present-day story, and a bank's everyday account is where money is kept.

clue.text: Dish, exquisite, and then some

parts.note: rare means exceptionally fine, exquisite
a bit means some, a little

explanation.surface: A dish that is exquisite and then some.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is a British dish of cheese sauce on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheese-on-toast dish is a savoury course, a kind of dish.

clue.text: Invalidate housing with old prison

indicators.note: housing means containing one piece inside another

parts.note: to negate is to invalidate

explanation.surface: Accommodation is cancelled for an old prison.
explanation.walkthrough: NEWGATE was a notorious London prison, closed in 1902.
explanation.definitionFit: The demolished London jail is an example of a former prison.

clue.text: Player often out of form?

parts.note: a sports player off form, but read as one who plays hooky and is often absent from a school form, or class

explanation.walkthrough: A 'form' is a British school class; one who 'plays' it is absent from school.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil who skips school without leave plays hooky, so is missing from class.

clue.text: What's spent on shooting game, a hundred for a penny originally

indicators.note: for means one letter stands in place of another

parts.note: partridge is a game bird
P is the abbreviation for a penny
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A shooting party's game birds cost a hundred pennies at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' says the penny's letter being swapped stands at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Once fired, a shell casing is described as spent, so it is what gets used up in shooting.

clue.text: Wife stuck in chestnut tree

indicators.note: stuck in means put inside

parts.note: a roan is a horse colour, like chestnut, used for a horse

explanation.surface: A wife is stuck up a chestnut tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chestnut tree' reads as one tree, but chestnut is a horse here.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain ash is a tree bearing red berries.

clue.text: Channel in Hebrew essentially making a comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An ancient language is essentially reviving.
explanation.definitionFit: A drain or conduit carries waste water, so it is a kind of channel.

clue.text: Move aside heading for exit, then duck accessing a way out

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter
accessing means getting into, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: LBW, leg before wicket, is one way a batsman is out in cricket
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: Someone pushes past to reach an exit while ducking through a way out.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket: LBW (leg before wicket) is a way of being given out, and a duck is a score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: To shove someone aside with the arm is a verb meaning push past.

clue.text: Capital of Honduras initially repackaged meat product

indicators.note: repackaged means the letters are rewrapped in another order
initially takes the first letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: The Honduran capital has had its meat products repackaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital of Honduras' reads as a city, but 'Capital' is anagram fodder, and 'initially' takes the first letters of 'of' and 'Honduras'.
explanation.definitionFit: A small thin sausage is a type of processed meat item.

clue.text: Prompt waiters, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: the phrase says the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a queue is a line of people waiting

explanation.surface: A diner hurries the waiters, by the sound of things.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's signal to speak is a prompt.

clue.text: Show point in West, perhaps

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: Mae West was a film star, an example of someone named West
a tine is a prong or point

explanation.surface: A point is made about the West.
explanation.definitionFit: An afternoon performance is a type of theatre show.

clue.text: Peak that's most difficult, not starting out

indicators.note: not starting means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: severest means most harsh or most difficult

explanation.surface: The hardest mountain is the one where you don't set off.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest mountain on Earth is a Himalayan summit.
